examples.en: That's an English keyboard.
Is that a new keyboard?
I type my name on the keyboard.
This keyboard is loud.

examples.ko: 한국어 키보드는 어디 있어요? — 저기 있어요.
examples.en: Where are the Korean keyboards? — Over there.

explain: 한국어 키보드에는 한글과 영어가 같이 있어요. 한/영 키로 바꿔요. 자음은 왼쪽, 모음은 오른쪽에 있어요.

phrases.example: 인터넷에서만 화를 내는 키보드 워리어가 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: used to mock someone who is aggressive only on the internet

explain_en: A Korean keyboard has Hangul and English on the same keys; switch with the 한/영 key. Consonants are on the left, vowels on the right.

examples.en: This is the laptop screen.
That over there is the cinema screen.
The screen is too small.
What's on the screen? — There's a photo.
The phone screen turns off.

explain: 화면은 컴퓨터, 휴대폰, TV에 모두 써요. 영화관의 큰 화면은 “스크린”이라고도 해요.

dict_examples.en: The screen is clear.

dict_examples.en: The newly bought TV has very vivid screen colors.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 화면 works for computers, phones and TVs alike. The big screen in a cinema is also called 스크린.

examples.en: The phone camera is really good.
This camera takes good pictures.
examples.extra_word: 나오다 = to come out (사진이 잘 나와요 = photos come out well)

examples.en: Do you have a camera? — Yes, on my phone.
I take photos with the camera.
I speak in front of the camera.

explain: 사진은 “찍다”와 같이 써요: 사진을 찍어요. 영어 take a picture의 take에 해당하는 말이 “찍다”예요.

phrases.en: camera shyness; nervousness in front of a camera
phrases.nuance_en: said lightly when you get nervous in front of a camera
phrases.en_equiv: camera shyness; nervousness in front of a camera

explain_en: Pictures go with 찍다: 사진을 찍어요. 찍다 is the Korean “take” in “take a picture”.

examples.en: One bottle of water, please.
I drank two bottles of beer yesterday.

examples.ko: 이 병 안에 뭐가 있어요? — 물이 있어요.
examples.en: What's in this bottle? — There's water.
I buy three bottles of juice at the shop.
I fill the bottle with water.

explain: 병은 bottle이면서 단위예요: 맥주 두 병. 소리가 같은 “병”(illness)도 있어요. 문장 안에서 뜻을 구별해요.

explain_en: 병 is both “bottle” and the counter for bottles: 맥주 두 병. There is another 병 meaning “illness”; the sentence tells you which.

examples.en: Is that a plate?
This is a cake plate.
I put food on the plate.
One more plate, please.
The plate is small. Please give me a bigger one.

explain: 접시는 음식의 양을 세는 말로도 써요: 전 한 접시, 회 한 접시. 한 접시에 담긴 만큼이라는 뜻이에요.

explain_en: 접시 also counts servings of food: 전 한 접시 (one plate of jeon), 회 한 접시 (one plate of sashimi). It means as much as fits on one plate.

examples.en: This is a spoon.
This is a baby spoon.
You eat rice with a spoon.
Is this a spoon? — No, it's chopsticks.
The baby uses a small spoon.

explain: 숟가락과 젓가락을 합쳐서 “수저”라고 해요. 식당에서 “수저 주세요”라고 하면 둘 다 줘요. 밥과 국은 보통 숟가락으로 먹어요.

phrases.example: 내가 다 했는데 친구가 숟가락만 얹었어요.
phrases.en: to take credit for others' work without contributing
phrases.nuance_ko: 남이 다 한 일에 슬쩍 끼어들 때 (비판)
phrases.nuance_en: a criticism of someone who slips into work that others have already done
phrases.en_equiv: to take credit for others' work without contributing

explain_en: Spoon and chopsticks together are called 수저. In a restaurant, 수저 주세요 gets you both. Rice and soup are usually eaten with the spoon.

examples.en: Those are chopsticks.
These are Korean chopsticks.
I eat side dishes with chopsticks.
I'm good with chopsticks.
Do you use chopsticks? — No, I use a fork.

explain: 한국 젓가락은 보통 쇠로 만들고 납작해요. 밥은 보통 숟가락으로 먹어요. 그래서 젓가락은 반찬을 집을 때 써요.

dict_examples.en: You must not stick chopsticks upright in rice.
dict_examples.src: AI 생성 · 검수

explain_en: Korean chopsticks are usually metal and flat. Rice is usually eaten with the spoon, so chopsticks are mainly for picking up side dishes.

examples.en: This is a mirror.
This is my hand mirror.
There's a big mirror in the restroom.
I brush my hair in front of the mirror.
I can see my face in the mirror.

explain: “Look in the mirror”는 “거울을 보다”예요. 몸 전체가 보이는 큰 거울은 “전신거울”이라고 해요.

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: She looks into the mirror day and night.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 아내는 거울 앞에 앉아 화장을 하고 있다.
dict_examples.en: My wife is sitting in front of the mirror putting on makeup.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: “Look in the mirror” is 거울을 보다. A big mirror that shows your whole body is a 전신거울.

examples.en: What's in that box?
This is a delivery box.

examples.ko: 상자 안에 뭐가 있어요? — 사과가 있어요.
examples.en: What's in the box? — There are apples.
This box is too heavy.
I put the present in the box.

explain: 상자와 “박스”는 같은 뜻이에요. 일상에서는 “박스”도 많이 써요: 택배 박스, 라면 한 박스.

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 소포로 배달된 상자 뚜껑을 여니 옷이 들어 있었다.
dict_examples.en: When I opened the lid of the box delivered as a parcel, there were clothes inside.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 상자 and 박스 mean the same. In daily life 박스 is also very common: 택배 박스 (delivery box), 라면 한 박스 (a box of ramen).

p.n: 박스 is a casual loanword, often for cardboard boxes; 상자 is the general word.
